text_simplified: This text discusses the rights of children upon their parents, mentioning some Prophetic hadiths that urge tarbiyah (upbringing) and teaching of children. It also highlights the importance of caring for the child from a young age and providing them with physical and psychological care. Parents must instill religious and moral values in the hearts of their children.

review_defects.why: The Arabic says 'health care' (رعاية صحية), which includes medical and overall health, but the English narrows it to 'physical care', omitting the health/medical dimension.
The Arabic verb 'تعزيز' means to strengthen or reinforce existing values, while 'instill' implies introducing values that are not yet present, changing the nuance.

review_defects.english: in the hearts of their children
review_defects.why: The Arabic 'نفوس' means souls or inner selves, not specifically 'hearts' (قلوب), so the English substitutes a different concept.
